found_values.value: One output of the I/O expander per biased line: 5 outputs, one each for the 4 multiprotocol ports and the UART socket. Each control input has a resistor that holds it at the pull-down selection, so the reset or unpowered state selects the pull-down (the condition in V57's answer). The expander resets with the RP2354B and its outputs then float (IOBoard.md:340), so the resistor sets the level. Why not the other choices: a jumper cannot follow the port's mode, which firmware sets per binding (IOBoard.md:64, :256). A circuit that follows the signal cannot tell the modes apart, because bidirectional DShot, ESC telemetry, bootloader and UART lines idle high and servo PWM and plain DShot idle low (IOBoard.md:251, :256, :273). An RP2354B GPIO would also meet V57, since its pads reset pulled low (RP2350 datasheet section 9.3), but it costs 5 GPIO
found_values.source: V57 answer (Research.md:617, owner 2026-09-28); IOBoard.md:64, :251, :256, :273, :340; RP2350 datasheet build 2025-07-29, section 9.3, https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/rp2350/rp2350-datasheet.pdf (served as RP-008373-DS-2 from pip-assets.raspberrypi.com)

found_values.value: With the pin released: the UART socket, and a multiprotocol port in ESC bootloader, ESC telemetry or servo configuration mode, take a pull-up of 1 kΩ to 3.3 V. The pull-up is switched by the bias selector and sits in parallel with the fixed 10 kΩ pull-down, which puts the idle at 3.0 V. With the gate disabled: the fixed 10 kΩ pull-down alone while the selector is at its reset or unpowered state (V57). While firmware keeps the pull-up selected, a disabled line idles at 3.0 V. Evidence: AM32's bootloader receives on an input with pull-up (main.c:516); at start-up it jumps to the application when the line reads mostly low against its own pull-down (main.c:1095-1121). BLHeli_S's bootloader drives its pin open-drain and high (BLHeliBootLoad.inc:71-72), so its high level comes from a pull-up alone. AM32's KISS telemetry on the G071 is open-drain with the MCU's pull-up (serial_telemetry.c:27-28). A Hitec D-series servo drives the line low only and has a 3 kΩ pull-down; the library needs a 1 kΩ pull-up to 3.3 V (HitecDServo README.md:10-11). OpenYGE is UART 8N1 and idles high (docs/OpenYGE.md:21). Why 1 kΩ: with the servo's 3 kΩ and the board's 10 kΩ pull-downs (2.31 kΩ together) the line sits at 3.3 × 2.31 / 3.31 = 2.30 V, above the 2.0 V V_IH of the RP2350 and of LVC inputs. A pull-up above 1.50 kΩ falls below 2.0 V
found_values.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/am32-firmware/AM32-bootloader/master/bootloader/main.c; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bitdump/BLHeli/master/BLHeli_S%20SiLabs/BLHeliBootLoad.inc; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/am32-firmware/AM32/main/Mcu/g071/Src/serial_telemetry.c; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/timmaxw/HitecDServo/main/README.md and src/HitecDServoInternal.h; docs/OpenYGE.md:21; RP2350 datasheet build 2025-07-29 Table 1436

found_values.value: The programmer (Hitec DPC-11) drives the line high at about 2 V and low at 0 V. The servo drives the line low only, and the programmer pulls it high at about 1.3 mA. The servo's input-high threshold is not stated; it reads the DPC-11's roughly 2 V as high. The library works from a 3.3 V microcontroller with a 1 kΩ pull-up to 3.3 V. Source status: the only source found is a reverse-engineered library that says it is not endorsed by Hitec. No Hitec publication of the protocol was found

One signal wire, the servo's PWM signal line, half duplex. UART with inverted polarity: idle low, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit. The servo's output is open-drain (drives low only), with a 3 kΩ pull-down inside the servo; the programmer supplies the pull-up. A servo that receives a serial command ignores PWM until it reboots. Same source status as V60
115,200 baud. Same source status as V60

3.3 V, driven from the 3.3 V rail on the 16 PWM ports, the 4 multiprotocol ports and the UART socket. No supply is sensed from the device. Evidence: ESCape32's signal line reads about 3.3 V. SRXL2 signals are 3.3 V logic. CRSF runs at 3.0 to 3.3 V. KISS telemetry is sent at 3.6 V. A Hitec D-series servo reads the DPC-11's roughly 2 V as high. No source read requires 5 V. The input thresholds of servos other than Hitec D-series are not read. The connector side must tolerate at least 3.6 V (the KISS level), with the board powered or unpowered
found_values.source: ESCape32 wiki Installation, step 4, https://github.com/neoxic/ESCape32/wiki/Installation; SRXL2 Specification Rev K, section 5, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SpektrumRC/SRXL2/master/Docs/SRXL2%20Specification.pdf; TBS CRSF spec crsf.md:134, :138, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tbs-fpv/tbs-crsf-spec/main/crsf.md; Betaflight src/main/sensors/esc_sensor.c:60; HitecDServoInternal.h

found_values.value: 1 kΩ to 3.3 V: the same switched pull-up as V58, in parallel with the fixed 10 kΩ pull-down, which puts the idle at 3.0 V. The pull-up only holds the idle, because both ESC firmwares read drive the reply push-pull: AM32 from a timer output (Mcu/g071/Src/IO.c:55-80), and Bluejay by setting its pin push-pull for the reply (src/Modules/Isrs.asm:481). AM32 targets pull the input up, except NEUTRONRC_G071, which pulls it down (Src/main.c:1930-1933). With the pull-up selected, the bench's driver sinks 3.3 mA while the line is low, within the RP2350 pad's 4 mA setting (V_OL ≤ 0.5 V, Table 1436). Hitec's servo configuration mode needs 1.50 kΩ or less, so one value serves every mode that idles high

1 receiver input. Each bus is one signal wire into one pin (docs/Receivers.md:10-16). The analyser screen takes one decoded frame stream (shared/ui/include/analyser_screen.h:27). No source read names a second input
found_values.source: docs/Receivers.md:10-16; shared/ui/include/analyser_screen.h:20-33 in the checkout at c25aa86

found_values.value: 3.3 V where a source states it: SRXL2 uses 3.3 V logic and idles at 3.3 V; CRSF uses 3.0 to 3.3 V. EX Bus states only a minimum logic one of 3.0 V and a maximum logic zero of 1.5 V, with no maximum high level. The documents read for SUMD (Graupner HoTT SUMD spec Rev 01) give no level. S.BUS and iBUS: no maker specification was read, so their level is not read
found_values.source: SRXL2 Specification Rev K section 5; crsf.md:134, :138; JETI EX Bus communication protocol v1.21 (18.12.2013), Physical layer, https://www.jetimodel.cz/uloz/c6d00c58-78ab-4c4d-9f15-34e84523479e.pdf/?1626095164; HoTT SUMD spec Rev 01, copy at https://www.deviationtx.com/media/kunena/attachments/98/HoTT-SUMD-Spec-REV01-12062012-pdf.pdf

found_values.value: 2,000,000 baud (CRSF). The single-wire half-duplex link defaults to 400 kbaud and supports 1 and 2 Mbaud depending on hardware (crsf.md:134); the full-duplex link defaults to 416,666 baud and can be negotiated higher (crsf.md:138). The other buses: SRXL2 400,000 baud (spec section 7.2); EX Bus 250,000 baud at high speed; SUMD 115,200 baud; S.BUS 100,000 baud. iBUS: not read
found_values.source: crsf.md:134, :138; SRXL2 Specification Rev K lines on the BaudRate field; EX Bus protocol v1.21 Physical layer; SUMD spec Rev 01 section on the data stream

found_values.value: No. The gate removes drive between the RP2350's output pins and the output connector (Monostable.md:361-367), and F13 names the 20 output ports and the UART socket. The bench transmits on the receiver input only telemetry to the receiver (EX Bus and SRXL2, V71), and a receiver input passes no drive to a servo or an ESC

Low, on every gated line, while the RP2354B is held in reset by RUN or by a brownout. In that state the pads have the output high-impedance and are pulled low at 36 to 113 kΩ (section 9.3; Table 1436). The gate element then passes, or buffers, a low; the connector's 10 kΩ pull-down holds it; the bias selector is at its reset selection. Low on a bidirectional DShot, bootloader or telemetry line is a constant level, which carries no frame. Through a watchdog reset the level is not determined by the datasheet: section 9.3 lists only brownout, RUN, SW-DP CDBGRSTREQ and RP-AP rescue reset as returning the pads to their reset state. Section 9.7 states that set isolation latches hold each pad's output enable, output level and pulls, and that the latches reset only on those always-on resets
found_values.source: RP2350 datasheet build 2025-07-29, sections 9.3 and 9.7, Table 1436; IOBoard.md:340

found_values.value: Yes, on the 4 multiprotocol ports, the UART socket and the receiver input. Devices can drive these lines from their own supply while the IO board is unpowered: a receiver on its own pack; SRXL2 devices on servo-bus power of 3.5 to 8.4 V (SRXL2 spec section 5); an ESC on the operator's pack during programming (V78). The RP2354B's fault-tolerant pins take only 3.63 V with IOVDD at 0 V (Table 1433), and the powered-off isolation rule covers every interlock input driven while its own supply is absent (Monostable.md:74-80)
found_values.source: SRXL2 Specification Rev K section 5; RP2350 datasheet build 2025-07-29 Table 1433; Monostable.md:74-80 at 23c82ca

found_values.value: Both faults, continuous: a short to ground, and a short to the port's supply pin at up to 8.7 V. The lead has signal, ground and rail in one plug (IOBoard.md:531), the rail reaches 8.7 V (F16), and nothing in the tree limits the current or the time of a signal fault (IOBoard.md:536). Derived series resistance 300 Ω per line (275 to 320 Ω). The lower bound: a short to ground draws at most 12 mA from the RP2354B pad (3.3 V / 275 Ω), the highest drive setting that Table 1436 characterises. The upper bound: in Hitec mode the RP2354B's low against the 1 kΩ pull-up stays below 0.8 V (3.3 × 300 / 1300 = 0.76 V). A short to 8.7 V puts (8.7 − 3.6) / 300 = 17 mA into a clamp at 3.6 V. The clamp is a part of round 2 (Research.md:28)
found_values.source: IOBoard.md:531, :536; F16 (Research.md:544); RP2350 datasheet build 2025-07-29 Table 1436; derivation above

found_values.value: Devices named: OpenYGE ESCs at 115,200 baud 8N1 (docs/OpenYGE.md:21), and the ESC telemetry protocols of the open decision in docs/OpenYGE.md:400-403 (Hobbywing, Kontronik, Scorpion, OMP, ZTW, APD, FLY, Graupner, XDFly), whose rates are not read. KISS telemetry runs at 115,200 baud. The highest rate found is 115,200 baud

KISS ESC telemetry on the ESC's separate telemetry wire, ESC to bench only, 115,200 baud 8N1, in 10-byte frames. AM32 sends it at 115,200 baud (serial_telemetry.c:53), open-drain on the G071 with the MCU's pull-up (lines 27-28), so the port takes the pull-up of V58. ESCape32's default telemetry mode is KISS (telem_mode 0). Highest baud found: 115,200
found_values.source: Betaflight esc_sensor.c:56-72, :113; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/am32-firmware/AM32/main/Mcu/g071/Src/serial_telemetry.c and Mcu/f051/Src/serial_telemetry.c; ESCape32 wiki Settings, https://github.com/neoxic/ESCape32/wiki/Settings

found_values.value: A STOP followed by the operator clear of the F11 latch; no separate switch. The ESC pack switch and the buffer enable both follow the enable node alone (Research.md:281-282). At the clear they rise together while the RP2354B already holds the line high, with the bootloader pull-up selected, so the ESC powers up with its line high. What the bootloaders need: AM32 stays in its bootloader only when the line does not read mostly low at start-up (main.c:1095-1125). BLHeli_S waits while the line is high and leaves after about 250 ms (BLHeliBootLoad.inc:10, :89-99). ESCape32 needs the line high for 2 s at start-up. A Hitec D-series servo needs no power cycle: it accepts serial 1000 ms after power-up, and firmware can reboot it through its REBOOT register (HitecDServoInternal.h). VESC's UART needs none
found_values.source: AM32-bootloader main.c; BLHeliBootLoad.inc; ESCape32 wiki Configuration; HitecDServoInternal.h; Research.md:281-282

report.value: A programming session powers the ESC up to enter its bootloader or CLI: AM32, BLHeli_S and ESCape32 need the line high at start-up. The bench does this with a STOP and the operator clear of the F11 latch, not with a firmware-driven switch: the ESC pack switch and the buffer enable both follow the enable node. A Hitec D-series servo needs no power cycle. VESC needs none
report.source: V78 found value; AM32-bootloader main.c:1095-1125 (13:18:40Z); BLHeliBootLoad.inc:10, :89-99 (13:18:41Z); ESCape32 wiki Configuration (12:52:40Z); HitecDServoInternal.h (12:54:16Z)

report.value: low on all 21 gated lines: the 16 PWM ports through SN74LVC244A, and the 4 multiprotocol ports and the UART socket through SN74CBTLV3126. The pads are at high impedance and pulled low at 36 to 113 kΩ; the 10 kΩ pull-downs hold the lines; the bias selector's reset state selects the pull-down

report.figure: connector level through a watchdog reset
report.value: not determined by the datasheet. Section 9.3 lists brownout, RUN, SW-DP CDBGRSTREQ and RP-AP rescue reset as returning the pads to their reset state; the watchdog is not listed. Section 9.7: set isolation latches hold each pad's output enable, level and pulls, and they reset only on those always-on resets. A line driving high before a watchdog reset can stay high while the gate stays enabled
report.source: RP2350 datasheet build 2025-07-29 sections 9.3 and 9.7, read 2026-09-28T13:12:51Z

report.value: SN74CBTLV3126 OE is active high and takes the active-high enable node directly, with a 10 kΩ pull-down at each OE pin. SN74LVC244A 1OE and 2OE are active low and take the node through SN74LVC1G04, with a 10 kΩ pull-up at each OE pin. Both agree with R3's enable node, which is high while retriggered (Monostable.md:422)
report.source: SCDS038N and SCAS414AG pin tables (read 13:03:55-56Z); Monostable.md:422 at 23c82ca

report.figure: GPIO and expander outputs for P5
report.value: The receiver input's SN74LVC1T45 needs 1 RP2354B GPIO for DIR. The bias selector needs 5 I/O expander outputs, one for each multiprotocol port and one for the UART socket (bears on V119). The switch path needs no direction pin, so the DShot PIO programs and their instruction counts are unchanged

The multiprotocol and UART lines are driven by the RP2354B pads through SN74CBTLV3126 and 300 Ω: V_OH ≥ 2.62 V and V_OL ≤ 0.5 V at the 2, 4, 8 or 12 mA setting. The 1 kΩ pull-up needs a 4 mA setting or higher

Parts were dropped when their datasheet gives Ioff for the data ports but no figure for the enable input at a supply of 0 V: TMUX1511 (fail-safe logic stated), SN74CB3Q3125, SN74LVC8T245 and TXU0104. SN74LVC126A states no Ioff at all. If the owner accepts a fail-safe-logic statement as I_off, TMUX1511PWR returns as the pin-compatible alternate of SN74CBTLV3126PWR (JLCPCB 4667, Digi-Key 0)
report.source: SCDS390B section 7.3.5; SCDS143E; SCES584D; SCES937B; SCAS339U (read 2026-09-28T13:03-13:17Z)
